What if all the oxygen in the air vanished for five seconds?
You'd think you would drop dead. You wouldn't.
You can hold your breath far longer than that.
But the air would suddenly be a fifth thinner. Your ears would pop, like shooting two kilometers up a mountain.
Every flame on Earth would go out. Candles, stoves, campfires.
Engines would cut out, because burning fuel needs oxygen.
Five seconds later, the oxygen is back. But a blown-out candle doesn't relight itself.
Now the scary version. If every oxygen atom vanished, water and rock would fall apart.
And so would you. Your body is about sixty-five percent oxygen.
